title: Chapter 6 — Ivie's Visit
description: A daughter with questions, a bar dressed up as a restaurant, and a dance war with Golden Fleece.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Saturday, 9 a.m. You have hung a banner over the gate: SUGAR'S KITCHEN. The girls are wearing aprons. Kokoro is wearing a chef's hat and an expression of deep betrayal.

beats.speaker: ivie
beats.text: (Running in, hugging you, smelling like school soap.) Mummy! It's so... (She looks at the stairs.) ...big. What is upstairs?

variants.text: (She is very still.) Is that how you paid for my school? (She doesn't cry. She is your daughter. She waits until the toilet to cry.)
(Long silence.) I knew something, Mummy. Girls at school have mothers. Some of them have mothers like you. (She takes your hand.) Thank you for not lying again.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You take a danfo to Ivie's school in Ikorodu with a nylon bag of provisions: Milo, Peak milk, cabin biscuits, and ₦10,000 folded inside the Milo tin like your mother used to do.

beats.speaker: ivie
beats.text: Mummy, you look tired. (She looks at your hands.) Why do your hands smell of beer?

beats.speaker: ivie
beats.text: She asked it lightly. She is not asking lightly.

options.text: "The restaurant sells drinks too, my love."
Tell her the truth, on the bench outside the dining hall.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Saturday night. Golden Fleece has hired a DJ and a generator the size of a danfo. Their best dancer, "Sweet Mother", is outside your gate, dancing at your customers until they cross the road.

beats.speaker: kokoro
beats.text: Mama, if we don't answer, by midnight every customer on this street will be drinking Rukky's beer.

won.toast: The customers cross back. Sweet Mother bows. Rukky does not.

beats.title: Ivie's Visit
beats.summary: Your daughter saw the house you built. Whatever she understood, she is taking it back to school with her.
